definition_simple: The city's online library where you can find all the public records for a property, like who bought it and for how much.
definition_technical: Automated City Register Information System - allows you to search property records and view document images for Manhattan, Queens, Bronx, and Brooklyn from 1966 to the present.
why_it_matters: Essential for checking if a house has any hidden legal problems or 'liens' before you buy it.

definition_technical: A sign showing goods or services available somewhere other than where the sign is erected. Largely prohibited in NYC residential areas. Small non-commercial signs (up to 12 sq ft for Sale/Rent) are permitted.
Construction or renovation work done before 7:00 AM or after 6:00 PM on weekdays, or anytime on weekends. Requires an After Hours Variance (AHV) permit.

A construction project that results in a new Certificate of Occupancy. Types: Type I (major CO changes like use conversions), Type II (multiple trades without use change), Type III (minor work like curb cuts). Work that doesn't trigger a new CO is classified as renovation instead.
A residential building containing four or more dwelling units, each with access to above-grade common halls, stairs, elevators, and yards.
A licensed professional like an architect or engineer who files construction plans with the city and ensures work meets all laws and codes.
A licensed professional who designs buildings and oversees construction projects. They create drawings, specifications, and ensure designs meet building codes.

A hazardous building material once commonly used for insulation and fireproofing. Inhaling fibers can cause lung cancer, mesothelioma, and asbestosis (effects appear 10-50 years later). Intact asbestos presents minimal danger, but disruption during renovations significantly increases hazards.
Converting attic space into habitable living area. Requires proper permits, egress windows, ceiling height, and may require structural reinforcement.

definition_simple: A surprise check by the city to make sure your architect or engineer really did follow all the rules.
definition_technical: [AI-DRAFT] A detailed review of construction documents by DOB to verify code compliance. Can result in objections that must be addressed before approval.
why_it_matters: If the city finds a mistake during an audit, you might have to stop work and fix it, which can be very expensive.

definition_technical: A financial institution that provides construction loans and mortgages for building projects. Banks underwrite loans based on project risk.
A floor level partly or fully below ground. In NYC, 'basement' often refers to illegal basement apartments that don't meet code requirements.

definition_simple: Buildings Information System - the city's old online database for looking up building info.
definition_technical: Buildings Information System - NYC Department of Buildings' free online tool where anyone can check property details, permits, violations, and complaints.
why_it_matters: You can use BIS to check for old violations or permits from years ago that might still be affecting a building.

definition_technical: NYC DOB issues several certificate types: Certificate of Occupancy (CO) confirms code compliance; Temporary CO (TCO) permits occupancy while work is pending; Certificate of Compliance verifies equipment code compliance; Elevator and Boiler Certificates prove inspection compliance.
The official document that confirms a violation has been fixed and stops the accumulation of penalties for unresolved violations.
[AI-DRAFT] A modification to a construction contract that changes the scope, cost, or timeline of a project. Often results from unforeseen conditions.
Categories used to classify DOB violations by severity: Class A (most dangerous, must be fixed immediately), Class B (hazardous), Class C (non-hazardous).

definition_simple: An office worker at the Department of Buildings who handles the initial paperwork.
definition_technical: [AI-DRAFT] A DOB employee who processes permit applications, maintains records, and handles administrative tasks at the Department of Buildings.
why_it_matters: They make sure your application is complete before it goes to the more senior experts for review.

definition_simple: It is an easy way for governments to keep track of issues reported by their constituents. This process allows the government to figure out if a problem is real or perceived.
definition_technical: A report filed with NYC agencies about building code issues, unsafe conditions, or illegal construction. Complaints may trigger inspections.
A professional hired to perform construction, repair, remodeling, or additions to buildings. In NYC, contractors working on residences must be licensed.
[AI-DRAFT] Official authorization required before tearing down a building or portion of a building. Involves safety reviews and environmental assessments.

NYC Department of Environmental Protection manages the city's water supply, sewers, wastewater treatment, and environmental rules. DEP can issue violations and fines for homeowner-caused issues like leaks or sewer backups that strain infrastructure.
A DOB enforcement mechanism allowing immediate stop-work orders and penalties for the most serious safety violations on construction sites.

Department of Buildings - NYC agency that reviews and approves building plans and permits, enforces building codes, licenses construction professionals, conducts inspections, and manages building emergencies. Failing to follow DOB requirements can result in violations, fines, stop-work orders, or eviction.

An online system created by the NYC Department of Buildings to make it easier for homeowners and professionals to handle building permits, inspections, and construction-related paperwork. Users can track permits, schedule inspections, and submit documents online.
NYC Department of Transportation - issues over 150 different types of sidewalk and roadway construction permits to utilities, contractors, government agencies, and homeowners.

definition_simple: The Environmental Control Board - the division of OATH that specificly handles building and environmental fines.
definition_technical: Environmental Control Board - a division of NYC's Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings (OATH) that holds hearings on violations issued by city agencies like DOB, DEP, and FDNY. ECB determines responsibility for violations and assesses fines as an independent tribunal.
why_it_matters: They set the final amount you have to pay for a violation based on the evidence presented in court.

definition_simple: The system for sending construction plans to the city electronically instead of bringing paper drawings to an office.
definition_technical: An online platform that property owners, architects, engineers, and contractors use to submit and manage building permit applications and other related filings in NYC.
why_it_matters: Makes the permit process much faster and easier to track for everyone involved.

definition_technical: [AI-DRAFT] A licensed professional who designs structural, mechanical, electrical, or plumbing systems for buildings. Works with architects to ensure buildings are safe and functional.

Environmental Protection Agency - federal agency (not NYC) that shapes what property owners must do to protect air, water, and environmental health. Enforces lead-based paint violations, drinking water contamination, asbestos and pesticide mishandling. EPA requirements supersede local DEP and DOB rules.

definition_simple: A person who is an expert at navigating the city's confusing paperwork and rules to get permits faster.
definition_technical: A DOB-registered filing representative (NYC expeditor) who streamlines building permit processes. They submit applications, present projects to DOB clerks and examiners, address objections, and coordinate approvals. With decades of experience, expeditors specialize in accelerating DOB and other agency approvals.
why_it_matters: They know exactly who to talk to at city agencies to get a project moving when it gets stuck.

definition_technical: [AI-DRAFT] The exterior face of a building, typically the front. Facade work includes repairs, cleaning, and decorative improvements to the building's exterior.
Not correcting a cited issue by the specified deadline and/or failing to certify the correction to the issuing agency. Results in escalating penalties.

definition_simple: The Fire Department of New York - they fight fires and provide emergency medical help.
definition_technical: Fire Department of New York - agency responsible for fire safety inspections, sprinkler and fire alarm permits, and fire code compliance.
why_it_matters: They are the primary protectors of life and property from fire in the city and also inspect buildings for fire safety.

definition_technical: [AI-DRAFT] The formal submission of construction documents, plans, and applications to DOB for review and approval. Different filing types include new building, alteration, and demolition.
[AI-DRAFT] The last stage of DOB review before a permit is issued or a certificate of occupancy is granted. Includes final document review and inspections.
Violations issued by FDNY for non-compliance with fire safety regulations including blocked exits, missing fire extinguishers, or faulty sprinkler systems.

definition_simple: Facade Inspection Safety Program - the law that says tall buildings must have their front walls checked every 5 years.
definition_technical: Facade Inspection Safety Program - NYC requirement for buildings over 6 stories to have their facades inspected every 5 years by a licensed professional.
why_it_matters: It's all about public safety; it prevents bricks or pieces of stone from falling off tall buildings and hitting people on the sidewalk.

definition_technical: A property requiring significant repairs or renovations before occupancy. Often purchased below market value with intent to renovate.

Building foundations rest on solid ground and spread the building's weight within safe limits for the soil. Must comply with NYC Building Code requiring proper soil support, adequate depth (typically 4 feet below frost line), and detailed geotechnical planning.

Owners must ensure gas meters remain in clean, dry locations free of refuse, at least 3 feet from hazards. Storage of combustibles prohibited within 5 feet. Natural gas piping is prone to leaks near meters.
[AI-DRAFT] Construction that incorporates environmentally sustainable practices including energy efficiency, renewable materials, and reduced environmental impact.

definition_simple: Department of Housing Preservation and Development - the agency that makes sure rental apartments are safe and well-kept.
definition_technical: Department of Housing Preservation and Development - NYC agency that issues violations when properties violate housing code standards, covering problems like broken equipment, leaks, poor hygiene, or pest issues.
aliases: Department of Housing Preservation and Development
why_it_matters: If your landlord doesn't provide heat or hot water, HPD is the agency that comes to help you.

definition_simple: Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning - the systems that keep a building comfortable and provide fresh air.
definition_technical: [AI-DRAFT] Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning - the mechanical systems that control a building's climate. HVAC work often requires permits and inspections.
why_it_matters: In New York, landlords are legally required to provide heat in the winter, and good ventilation is key to stopping the spread of mold and germs.

definition_technical: Converting a space to residential use without proper permits or in violation of zoning laws. Common examples include converting basements, attics, or commercial spaces to apartments.
The DOB term for occurrences caused by construction or demolition activity that may or may not result in injury, such as structural failures, equipment collapses, or near-misses.
An official examination of construction work by DOB, FDNY, or other agencies to verify compliance with approved plans and building codes.

NYC inspectors check homes to keep them safe and ensure they follow city rules. DOB inspectors oversee construction, zoning, and major repairs. HPD housing inspectors handle rentals for heat, hot water, pests, leaks, lead paint, and smoke detectors. Both enforce codes through scheduled or surprise visits.
[AI-DRAFT] An individual or organization that provides capital for construction projects in exchange for ownership stake or expected returns.
Horizontal structural members that support floors and ceilings. Joists transfer loads to beams and walls. Common in wood-frame and steel construction.

A living room used for cooking with 80+ square feet of floor area, classifying it as habitable space requiring light and air. NYC kitchens must have proper ventilation, sink with running water, and fire-retarded materials.

definition_simple: Limited Alteration Application - a simplified permit process for small repair jobs, like fixing a leaky pipe.
definition_technical: Limited Alteration Application - a DOB filing method used for minor alterations with a defined scope of work, such as correcting plumbing violations.
why_it_matters: Allows simple repairs to be approved almost immediately so work can get done without long delays.

definition_simple: A high-level award for buildings that are built to be super eco-friendly and energy-efficient.
definition_technical: [AI-DRAFT] Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design - a green building certification program that rates buildings on sustainability, energy efficiency, and environmental impact.
aliases: Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design
why_it_matters: LEED buildings save the owner money on electricity and water and are better for the environment.

definition_simple: Licensed Master Plumber - a pro who has passed hard tests and is licensed to do any plumbing work in the city.
definition_technical: Licensed Master Plumber - a qualified professional required to perform plumbing work and submit necessary paperwork to the DOB in NYC.
why_it_matters: In NYC, only an LMP can legally sign the papers needed to get a plumbing permit.

definition_technical: [AI-DRAFT] Borrowed money used to finance construction projects. Construction loans are typically short-term and convert to mortgages upon project completion.

definition_simple: Letter of Completion - a final document from the city saying a construction job was finished correctly.
definition_technical: Letter of Completion - a document issued by DOB confirming that construction work has been completed in accordance with approved plans and permits.
why_it_matters: It's the official 'mission accomplished' for a renovation project, meaning all the permits are closed and the work is legal.

definition_simple: Multiple Dwelling Law - the statewide rules for buildings with 3 or more apartments.
definition_technical: Multiple Dwelling Law - NY State statute defining 'private dwellings' (1-2 families) and 'multiple dwellings' (3+ families). Class A = permanent residence (30+ days), Class B = transient occupancy (hotels). Imposes rules on design, safety, fire protection, and occupancy.
why_it_matters: This law is why apartment buildings have fire escapes and why landlords must keep the hallways lit and safe.

definition_technical: [AI-DRAFT] The non-structural systems in a building including HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and fire protection. Mechanical work requires specialized permits.
[AI-DRAFT] A building or project that combines residential, commercial, and/or industrial uses. Common in urban areas to maximize land use efficiency.
A fungal growth that can develop in damp building conditions. Mold remediation may require professional handling and can be cited as an HPD violation.
[AI-DRAFT] The process of discussing terms between parties in a construction project, such as contract terms, change orders, or dispute resolution.
An official document sent by a NYC agency to inform a property owner that something on their property might not follow local building or safety codes.

definition_simple: New York City Housing Authority - the agency that provides public housing for thousands of New Yorkers.
definition_technical: New York City Housing Authority - the largest public housing authority in North America, managing affordable housing for over 400,000 residents across 335 developments. Also administers Section 8 vouchers for 235,000+ people in private rentals.
why_it_matters: The largest provider of affordable housing in the city, helping families with low and moderate incomes.

definition_simple: The city's independent 'court' where building violations and fines are decided.
definition_technical: Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings - NYC's central, independent administrative law court that handles hearings for violations issued by city agencies.
aliases: Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings
why_it_matters: If you get a building fine, you go to OATH to argue your case before an independent judge.

definition_technical: [AI-DRAFT] The property owner who initiates and funds a construction project. The owner hires professionals like architects, engineers, and contractors.
[AI-DRAFT] Financial fines imposed for building code violations. Penalties can accumulate daily until violations are corrected and certified.

Official authorization from NYC's Department of Buildings allowing construction, alteration, demolition, or related work. Permits ensure compliance with building codes, safety regulations, and zoning laws. Types include New Building, Alteration (Types 1-3), and specialized permits.
[AI-DRAFT] The DOB review process where examiners check construction plans for code compliance. Can result in objections that must be resolved before approval.
[AI-DRAFT] A DOB employee who reviews construction plans and drawings to ensure they comply with building codes before issuing permits.
[AI-DRAFT] The water supply and drainage systems in a building. Plumbing work requires permits and must be performed by licensed plumbers.
Violations when plumbing systems fail to meet NYC Plumbing Code standards. Common causes: improper drain slopes, missing clean-outs, incorrect fittings or materials, inadequate fixture clearance.
[AI-DRAFT] A faster DOB approval path where a licensed professional certifies that plans comply with code, bypassing standard plan examination. Subject to audit.
[AI-DRAFT] The professional responsible for overseeing a construction project from start to finish, coordinating between owner, designers, and contractors.

Records containing Block & Lot information, existing legal plans, violation copies, sales history, parcel number, title changes, liens, square footage, year built, permits, zoning, and historical records of repairs and alterations.

definition_simple: The main form used to apply for a building permit in NYC.
definition_technical: Plan/Work Application - the primary DOB application form for getting approval of construction plans and work. Required for most building projects.
why_it_matters: It's the first page of any permit application and lists the owner, the architect, and the overall scope of the work.

definition_simple: Qualified Exterior Wall Inspector - a high-level architect or engineer who is an expert at checking building walls for safety.
definition_technical: Qualified Exterior Wall Inspector - a Registered Architect or Professional Engineer certified by DOB to perform exterior wall inspections under the Facade Inspection & Safety Program (FISP/Local Law 11).
why_it_matters: Only a QEWI can do the official inspections required for the FISP (Facade) program to make sure building fronts aren't dangerous.

definition_technical: Real Estate Board of New York - leading trade association founded in 1896 representing property owners, builders, managers, investors, and brokers. Establishes industry standards and advocates for real estate policies across NYC.
aliases: Real Estate Board of New York

definition_technical: Any improvement, modification, or repair work done to a property - interiors, exteriors, structural elements, or building systems. Must comply with NYC building codes and typically requires permits. Illegal renovation = work done without proper documentation and permits.

Describes the use or occupancy of a building or zoning district type. Becomes relevant when DOB rules, permits, violations, or exemptions depend on whether a building is classified as residential rather than commercial or industrial.
[AI-DRAFT] Upgrading an existing building with new or improved systems, such as energy-efficient equipment or seismic improvements.

Temporary elevated platforms for construction work. NYC requires permits for supported scaffolds over 40 feet and for sidewalk sheds. 2025 standards require 12 feet minimum height and adequate lighting.
[AI-DRAFT] The defined extent of work in a construction project, including what will be built, modified, or demolished. Changes to scope affect cost and timeline.
[AI-DRAFT] Structural modifications to make existing buildings more resistant to earthquakes. Required in some areas for certain building types.
[AI-DRAFT] Fire suppression systems that automatically release water when fire is detected. Sprinkler installation requires FDNY permits and inspections.

definition_simple: Stop Work Order - a red sign taped to a building by an inspector that says all construction must stop immediately.
definition_technical: Stop Work Order - an order issued when construction or repair work must be stopped because inspectors found unsafe conditions or work that could be dangerous.
why_it_matters: The city issues an SWO when they find something very dangerous; if you keep working after an SWO, you can be arrested or heavily fined.

definition_technical: A construction technique to strengthen or deepen existing foundations. Required when excavating near existing buildings or when foundations are inadequate.
[AI-DRAFT] The process by which a bank or lender evaluates a construction project's risk and determines loan terms, amount, and interest rate.
Work or installations completed without proper authorization or permits from NYC authorities. Unpermitted work can result in violations and fines.
A structure that poses risks to occupants or the public due to structural defects, fire hazards, or other dangerous conditions.
[AI-DRAFT] An exception to zoning rules granted by the city allowing a property to be used in a way not normally permitted. Requires approval from the Board of Standards and Appeals.

Notices issued by NYC agencies such as DOB, ECB, and HPD for non-compliance with building, housing, safety, or environmental codes. Violation classes: Class A (most dangerous - fix immediately), Class B (hazardous - 30 days), Class C (non-hazardous - 90 days).

Work Without a Permit - construction or alteration work performed without obtaining the necessary DOB permit. The most common violation type in NYC building code enforcement. Can result in fines, mandatory corrections, and additional penalties if hazardous conditions are present.
[AI-DRAFT] Local laws that regulate how land and buildings can be used in different areas. Zoning determines what can be built, how tall, and what uses are permitted.
Expert advice and services related to understanding and complying with the NYC Zoning Resolution and other building codes.
The agency responsible for fire protection and emergency medical services in New York City.
A legal order from a government agency that requires construction or other work to be halted, typically due to safety or compliance issues.
The greenhouse gas emissions produced by a building
The amount of greenhouse gases released into the atmosphere by a building.

definition_simple: A city program that helps people with disabilities get government jobs.
definition_technical: A program that allows the City of New York to hire individuals with disabilities, even if they do not meet the minimum qualifications for a civil service title.
why_it_matters: Makes sure the city workforce is inclusive and gives everyone a fair chance to serve the public.

definition_simple: A city program that helps people with disabilities get government jobs.
definition_technical: A New York City program that provides employment opportunities for individuals with disabilities.
why_it_matters: Makes sure the city workforce is inclusive and gives everyone a fair chance to serve the public.

definition_simple: The most important document for a building; it proves that the city has checked the building and said it is safe to live in.
definition_technical: A document issued by the Department of Buildings that certifies a building or structure is in compliance with applicable building codes and can be legally occupied.
why_it_matters: You cannot legally live in or sell a new or majorly renovated building without this certificate.

definition_simple: The most important document for a building; it proves that the city has checked the building and said it is safe to live in.
definition_technical: A document issued by a local government agency or building department certifying that a building or structure complies with applicable building codes and regulations and can be legally occupied.
why_it_matters: You cannot legally live in or sell a new or majorly renovated building without this certificate.

definition_simple: The Department of Citywide Administrative Services - the agency that manages city buildings and hires city workers.
definition_technical: The New York City Department of Citywide Administrative Services is an agency responsible for managing the civil service system, city real estate, and providing support services to other city agencies.
category: the agency responsible for the civil service system in New York City.
why_it_matters: They are the 'back office' of the city, making sure other agencies have the space and people they need to work.

definition_technical: A specialized financial institution that works in market niches that are underserved by traditional financial institutions.
A NYC regulatory program that requires periodic inspections and repairs of building facades to ensure public safety.
A temporary structure erected over a sidewalk to protect pedestrians from falling debris during construction or facade work.
A DOB initiative to reduce the number of unnecessary and long-standing sidewalk sheds across NYC.
The NYC law that established the Facade Inspection & Safety Program (FISP).

definition_simple: Latest updates about how seafood is checked for safety and quality in New York City.
definition_technical: Information regarding the regulatory inspections and compliance standards for seafood products as mandated by the International Aquatic and Terrestrial Certification agency.
why_it_matters: Ensures that seafood consumed in the city meets health standards and is safe for the public.

definition_simple: News and updates related to trade and commerce in the aquatic and terrestrial industries from the International Aquatic and Terrestrial Certification (IATC) agency.
definition_technical: News and updates related to trade and commerce in the aquatic and terrestrial industries from the International Aquatic and Terrestrial Certification (IATC) agency.

definition_simple: New York City's official program for sidewalk and roadway cafes.
definition_technical: The permanent outdoor dining program managed by the NYC Department of Transportation, replacing the temporary pandemic-era measures with standardized design and accessibility requirements.
why_it_matters: It sets the rules for how restaurants can use outdoor space, affecting neighborhood character and sidewalk accessibility.

definition_simple: The metal roll-down gates used to protect store windows and doors when they are closed.
definition_technical: A movable barrier used for securing commercial premises, which in NYC must typically provide at least 75% transparency when closed to comply with zoning regulations.
why_it_matters: Businesses use them for safety, but NYC has rules about how much they must be see-through to keep streets looking safe and inviting.

definition_simple: The giant book of rules that says what can be built where in New York City.
definition_technical: The comprehensive set of regulations governing land use and development in New York City, divided into zoning districts that specify permitted uses, bulk, and density.
why_it_matters: It determines if a building can be a house, a store, or a factory, and how tall it can be.

definition_simple: The big metal box that circulates and cleans the air in a building's heating and cooling system.
definition_technical: A device used to regulate and circulate air as part of a heating, ventilating, and air-conditioning system, typically containing a blower, heating/cooling elements, and filters.
why_it_matters: It is the 'lungs' of the building, ensuring fresh air and comfortable temperatures for occupants.

definition_simple: A change or update made to a building plan that has already been submitted to the city.
definition_technical: A request to modify a previously filed application or approved construction documents.
why_it_matters: Allows architects and owners to fix mistakes or change designs without starting the whole permit process over.

definition_simple: A yearly check-up required for certain building systems like elevators or boilers to make sure they are safe.
definition_technical: A mandatory periodic examination of building equipment and systems to ensure ongoing compliance with safety codes and operational standards.
why_it_matters: Prevents accidents and ensures that critical building machinery is working correctly and safely.

definition_simple: When a construction project follows all the rules perfectly and doesn't need any special permissions from the city.
definition_technical: A development that complies with all applicable zoning regulations and does not require a discretionary action such as a variance or special permit.
why_it_matters: As-of-right projects are much faster and cheaper because they don't need public hearings or special board approvals.

definition_simple: A licensed professional who tests buildings for dangerous asbestos fibers before renovation or demolition.
definition_technical: An individual certified by the NYC Department of Environmental Protection to perform asbestos surveys and hazard assessments.
why_it_matters: Disrupting asbestos can cause severe lung diseases; investigators make sure it's found and handled safely.

definition_simple: A roof-like cover, usually made of fabric, that sticks out over a window or door to provide shade.
definition_technical: A secondary covering attached to the exterior wall of a building, typically composed of canvas woven of acrylic, cotton or polyester yarn.
why_it_matters: Awnings improve energy efficiency and storefront appearance, but they must meet size and safety rules to avoid fines.

definition_simple: A very large outdoor sign used for advertising, often found on high buildings or near highways.
definition_technical: A large outdoor advertising structure, often classified as an indirect business sign or advertising sign under NYC zoning law.
why_it_matters: NYC has strict rules about where billboards can be placed to prevent light pollution and preserve neighborhood character.

definition_simple: A type of roof support that looks like a curved bow, often found in older warehouses and garages.
definition_technical: A structural truss having a curved top chord and a straight bottom chord, once common in large-span roof construction but prone to sudden failure under high heat.
why_it_matters: These roofs can be very dangerous during a fire because they can collapse suddenly without warning.

definition_simple: The Board of Standards and Appeals - the city agency that can grant 'exceptions' to zoning rules.
definition_technical: A New York City agency with the authority to grant variances from the Zoning Resolution and to hear appeals of determinations made by the Department of Buildings.
why_it_matters: If a property owner can't follow zoning rules because of unique problems with their land, the BSA can help them get a variance.

definition_simple: A plan that shows how a builder will fix or build the sidewalks and curbs around a new building.
definition_technical: A submission to the NYC Department of Transportation (DOT) and Department of Buildings (DOB) detailing the design and construction of sidewalks, curbs, and other public right-of-way improvements.
why_it_matters: Ensures that new construction leaves the public sidewalks safe, level, and properly drained.

definition_simple: The 'skin' of a building that keeps the weather out, including the walls, roof, windows, and doors.
definition_technical: The physical separator between the conditioned and unconditioned environment of a building, including the resistance to air, water, heat, light, and noise transfer.
why_it_matters: A good envelope keeps the building energy-efficient, dry, and comfortable.

definition_simple: A unique 7-digit number given to every building in New York City (like a social security number for buildings).
definition_technical: A unique seven-digit identifier assigned to every building in NYC, used for tracking all Department of Buildings records and filings.
why_it_matters: It is the best way to look up a building's history, permits, and violations in the city's database.

definition_simple: A permanent roof-like structure made of metal or glass that covers an entrance or walkway.
definition_technical: A fixed shelter or covering extending over a doorway or window, often constructed of rigid materials and requiring specific permits from the Department of Transportation.
why_it_matters: Canopies provide protection from rain and snow but require DOT permits because they hang over public sidewalks.

definition_simple: An outdoor parking space for a car that has a roof but no walls (unlike a garage).
definition_technical: An open-sided automobile shelter, usually formed by an extension of a roof from the side of a building or a freestanding roofed structure.
why_it_matters: They are cheaper than garages but still need to follow zoning and fire safety rules to prevent fire spread between houses.

definition_simple: The official form you send to the city to prove that you fixed a building violation.
definition_technical: The formal documentation submitted to the Department of Buildings to certify that the conditions cited in a violation have been remediated.
why_it_matters: Just fixing the problem isn't enough; you must file this form to stop the fines from growing.

definition_simple: The final part of a construction project where all paperwork is finished and the final inspections are done.
definition_technical: The final stage of a project involving the completion of all administrative and technical requirements to obtain a Letter of Completion or Certificate of Occupancy.
why_it_matters: This is when you get your final Certificate of Occupancy, allowing you to legally use or sell the building.

definition_simple: When a building or design follows all the safety and construction laws perfectly.
definition_technical: Meeting all the requirements of the NYC Building Code, Fire Code, and other applicable local regulations.
why_it_matters: Ensures the building is safe for people to live in and avoids costly fines or stop-work orders.

definition_simple: Describes a building or area used for business, like offices, stores, or restaurants.
definition_technical: A property classification used for businesses and industries, as opposed to residential or industrial use.
why_it_matters: Commercial buildings have different rules for taxes, zoning, and safety than residential houses.

definition_simple: A high-tech test to make sure a building's systems (like heating and cooling) are working as efficiently as the designers promised.
definition_technical: A quality-focused process for enhancing the delivery of a project by verifying and documenting that the facility and all of its systems and assemblies are planned, designed, installed, tested, operated, and maintained to meet the owner's project requirements.
why_it_matters: Saves energy costs and ensures that complex building systems are actually doing their job correctly.

definition_simple: A small room in larger buildings where trash is crushed before being picked up.
definition_technical: A dedicated space within a building for the collection and mechanical compaction of refuse, subject to specific health and fire code requirements.
why_it_matters: These rooms must have special fire sprinklers and ventilation because they are high fire risks and can smell.

definition_simple: The process of building, repairing, or changing any part of a building.
definition_technical: The act or process of building, altering, or repairing a structure, typically requiring a sequence of permits, inspections, and approvals.
source_url: What Is Construction? [Different Types & Importance] | Go Construct
why_it_matters: Construction is the foundation of city growth but must be carefully managed to keep workers and neighbors safe.

definition_simple: The final blueprints and instructions used by builders to actually construct a project.
definition_technical: The detailed drawings and specifications created by architects or engineers that form the basis for building permit applications and construction contracts.
why_it_matters: The city reviews these documents to make sure the building will be safe and follow all laws.

definition_simple: The temporary wall (often made of wood) built around a construction site to keep people out and keep them safe.
definition_technical: A temporary structure required around construction or demolition sites to provide security and protect the public from hazards.
why_it_matters: Protects the public from falling debris and prevents unauthorized people from entering dangerous areas.

definition_simple: The person in charge of daily work at a construction site who makes sure everything is safe and follows the plans.
definition_technical: A person registered with the Department of Buildings who is responsible for safety and code compliance on a construction site.
why_it_matters: They are legally responsible for safety; if someone gets hurt, they are the first person the city looks to.

definition_simple: An expert hired to give advice on tricky parts of a project, like zoning, energy, or historical preservation.
definition_technical: A professional provider of specialized advice or services related to the construction, legal, or financial aspects of property development.
why_it_matters: Helps owners navigate complex city rules and find ways to save time and money.

definition_simple: When a building's use is changed, like turning an old factory into apartments.
definition_technical: A change in the use or occupancy of a building or a portion thereof from one classification to another.
why_it_matters: Conversions usually require a new Certificate of Occupancy and must meet strict new safety rules.

definition_simple: A signed document telling the city exactly how much a construction project costs.
definition_technical: A formal statement of the estimated or actual cost of a project, used by the Department of Buildings to determine filing fees.
why_it_matters: The city uses this number to calculate how much you have to pay for your building permits.

definition_simple: A break in the sidewalk curb that allows cars to drive over the sidewalk into a driveway.
definition_technical: A dip in the sidewalk and curb allowing vehicular access to a property, requiring approval from both the DOT and DOB.
why_it_matters: Needs a special permit because it removes a parking spot from the street and can be dangerous for pedestrians.

definition_simple: The official height of the sidewalk curb in front of a building.
definition_technical: The elevation of the street curb at the center of the front of a building, used as a reference point for building height and bulk measurements.
why_it_matters: Architects use this level to measure how tall a building is allowed to be under zoning rules.

definition_simple: A check-up by the city to see how badly a building was damaged after a fire, storm, or accident.
definition_technical: The evaluation of structural integrity and safety following an incident to determine if a building can remain occupied.
why_it_matters: Determines if a building is safe to enter or if people need to be evacuated immediately.

definition_simple: The Department of City Planning - the agency that writes the zoning rules for the whole city.
definition_technical: The New York City agency responsible for the city's physical and socioeconomic planning, including the maintenance of the Zoning Resolution.
why_it_matters: They decide which neighborhoods can have big apartment buildings and which should stay small houses.

definition_simple: The trash and waste left over from construction or demolition work.
definition_technical: Waste materials resulting from construction, remodeling, or demolition activities.
why_it_matters: Must be cleaned up and hauled away correctly to prevent fires and keep neighbors safe.

definition_simple: An outdoor platform, usually made of wood or plastic, where people can sit and relax.
definition_technical: A floor-like platform, typically elevated and attached to a building, subject to structural and zoning regulations.
why_it_matters: Decks need permits if they are above a certain size or height to make sure they won't collapse or catch fire easily.

definition_simple: The process of tearing down a building or a part of it.
definition_technical: The complete or partial removal of a structure, requiring specialized permits and adherence to rigorous safety standards.
why_it_matters: Extremely dangerous work that needs special permits, safety fences, and dust control to protect neighbors.

definition_simple: The stage of a project where architects turn a rough idea into a detailed plan.
definition_technical: The phase in which the project design is refined, selecting materials and finalizing systems before creating construction documents.
why_it_matters: This is when the owner decides on materials and layouts before the final blueprints are drawn.

definition_simple: A rule that allows architects and engineers to do their own final inspections instead of waiting for a city inspector.
definition_technical: A DOB regulation allowing licensed professionals to certify that a completed project complies with approved plans.
why_it_matters: Saves weeks or months of waiting time, helping projects get finished faster.

definition_simple: The Department of Buildings' new online system for all construction filings.
definition_technical: The modernized, web-based portal used by the NYC Department of Buildings for permit applications, inspections, and public records.
why_it_matters: Property owners and architects use this website to submit almost all paperwork to the city today.

definition_simple: A person who creates technical drawings and blueprints for buildings.
definition_technical: An individual skilled in technical drawing who assists in the creation of architectural and engineering plans.
why_it_matters: They help architects and engineers put their ideas onto paper so that builders can understand them.

definition_simple: A private road that leads from the street to a house or garage.
definition_technical: A private access way for vehicles, connecting a property to the public street, subject to specific dimensional and surfacing rules.
why_it_matters: Driveways must follow zoning rules so they don't block sidewalks or take up too much yard space.

definition_simple: Any building or part of a building where people live.
definition_technical: A structure or portion thereof which is occupied in whole or in part as the home, residence, or sleeping place of one or more persons.
why_it_matters: Dwellings have much stricter rules for light, air, and fire safety than office buildings.

definition_simple: The number of separate apartments or houses in a building.
definition_technical: A single unit providing complete, independent living facilities for one or more persons, including permanent provisions for living, sleeping, eating, cooking, and sanitation.
why_it_matters: Adding more units often requires a new Certificate of Occupancy and can trigger major new safety rules.

definition_simple: A legal right for someone else to use a part of your land for a specific reason (like a utility company having a pipe under your yard).
definition_technical: A right to cross or otherwise use someone else's land for a specified purpose.
why_it_matters: You can't build anything permanent on an easement, which might limit where you can put an extension or a fence.

definition_simple: A safe way to get out of a building, especially during an emergency like a fire.
definition_technical: A continuous and unobstructed way of exit travel from any point in a building or structure to a public way.
why_it_matters: Every room where someone sleeps must have a safe 'way out' (like a window or door) to save lives during a fire.

definition_simple: The system of wires, outlets, and lights that provides power to a building.
definition_technical: The installation, maintenance, and repair of electrical wiring, equipment, and fixtures in a building.
why_it_matters: Faulty wiring is a leading cause of house fires; all electrical work must be done by a licensed pro and checked by the city.

definition_simple: The machine that carries people up and down between floors in a building.
definition_technical: A type of vertical transportation machine that moves people or goods between floors, levels, or decks of a building.
why_it_matters: Elevators must be inspected every year because a breakdown can trap people or cause serious injury.

definition_simple: When the city says a building is so dangerous that it must be fixed or evacuated immediately.
definition_technical: An official determination by the Commissioner of Buildings that a building condition is imminently perilous to life or property.
why_it_matters: Protects lives when a building is at risk of falling down or has a major gas leak.

definition_simple: Back-up power (like a generator) that keeps lights and elevators working when the main electricity goes out.
definition_technical: An independent source of electrical power which supports important electrical systems on loss of normal power supply.
why_it_matters: Crucial for high-rise buildings so people can get out safely during a blackout.

definition_simple: When a building or structure (like a fence or a stoop) sticks out into someone else's land or onto the public sidewalk.
definition_technical: An unauthorized intrusion or extension of a structure or improvement onto an adjoining property or public right-of-way.
why_it_matters: Illegal encroachments can lead to lawsuits between neighbors or fines from the city for blocking the sidewalk.

definition_simple: The city's way of making sure people follow building laws, often by issuing fines or stop-work orders.
definition_technical: The process of ensuring compliance with laws, regulations, and codes through inspections, citations, and legal actions.
why_it_matters: Ensures that everyone builds safely and fairly, protecting the whole neighborhood.

definition_simple: A special permission from the city to use a specific machine in a building, like a large boiler or an air conditioner.
definition_technical: An authorization issued by the Department of Buildings for the operation of certain service equipment.
why_it_matters: Ensures that powerful machines are installed correctly so they don't explode or cause fires.

definition_simple: Digging deep holes in the ground to prepare for a new building foundation.
definition_technical: The removal of soil or rock from a site to form a cavity or hole, typically for the construction of foundations.
why_it_matters: The most dangerous part of construction; if done wrong, it can make the buildings next door collapse.

definition_simple: The front or outside 'face' of a building.
definition_technical: The exterior face of a building, including walls, windows, and decorative elements.
why_it_matters: NYC has a law (Local Law 11) that requires old buildings to have their facades checked so bricks don't fall on people walking below.

definition_simple: The formal paperwork you send to the Department of Buildings to get a construction permit.
definition_technical: The initial submission of project details and construction documents to the Department of Buildings for review.
why_it_matters: The first step in any legal construction project; without it, the work is illegal.

definition_simple: Automatic systems, like sprinklers, that put out fires without human help.
definition_technical: An engineered set of components designed to detect and extinguish or control fires automatically.
why_it_matters: These systems save lives and protect property by stopping fires while they are still small.

definition_simple: The very early stage of a project where you figure out if what you want to build is possible and how much it will cost.
definition_technical: The process of developing sufficient information for owners to address risks and make decisions to commit resources to a project.
why_it_matters: Good planning at the start prevents expensive surprises and mistakes later on.

definition_simple: The system of pipes that carries natural gas for cooking and heating.
definition_technical: The installation and maintenance of pipes and fittings used to convey natural gas from the meter to appliances.
why_it_matters: Gas leaks are extremely dangerous; all gas work must be tested and approved by both the city and the utility company.

definition_simple: A roof that is partially or completely covered with plants.
definition_technical: A layer of vegetation grown on a rooftop, providing environmental benefits such as reduced urban heat island effect and improved insulation.
why_it_matters: They help cool the building, absorb rainwater to prevent flooding, and make the city look better.

definition_simple: A safety rail or fence built near the edge of a roof, stairs, or balcony to keep people from falling.
definition_technical: A railing system designed to prevent people or objects from falling from a higher level to a lower level.
why_it_matters: Must be exactly the right height and strength to prevent accidental falls and comply with safety codes.

definition_simple: A powerful machine or elevator used to lift heavy materials and workers up to high floors during construction.
definition_technical: A mechanical device used for lifting or lowering a load by means of a drum or lift-wheel around which rope or chain wraps.
why_it_matters: Needs regular safety checks because a failure can drop thousands of pounds of material.

definition_simple: A high-priority order from the city to fix a building problem that could kill someone right now.
definition_technical: A formal order issued when a building condition is determined to be an immediate danger to public safety.
why_it_matters: Allows the city to hire its own contractors to fix the problem immediately if the owner refuses.

definition_simple: A building or area that is officially protected because it is historic or beautiful.
definition_technical: A building, structure, or site that is officially recognized by the city for its historical, architectural, or cultural significance.
why_it_matters: You need special permission (from the Landmarks Preservation Commission) to change anything on the outside of a landmarked building.

definition_simple: A special pit or area where a tunnel-boring machine starts digging.
definition_technical: An excavation created to initiate the drive of a tunnel-boring machine.
why_it_matters: Requires major excavation and safety plans to prevent the street above from sinking.

definition_simple: A document from the city saying they have no problem with a building being used for a specific purpose (even if there is no official certificate).
definition_technical: An official letter from the DOB confirming that the current use of a building is legal based on historical records, even without a modern Certificate of Occupancy.
why_it_matters: Useful for older buildings that were built before certificates of occupancy were even invented.

definition_simple: Rules that say every bedroom must have a window that lets in natural light and fresh air.
definition_technical: Minimum legal requirements for natural illumination and ventilation in habitable rooms, as defined by the NYC Building Code and Multiple Dwelling Law.
why_it_matters: Prevents the creation of dark, windowless 'closet' bedrooms that are unhealthy and illegal.

definition_simple: The horizontal support beam above a window or door opening.
definition_technical: A horizontal structural member that spans an opening between two vertical supports, such as a door or window.
why_it_matters: If lintels get rusty and weak, they can break and cause the bricks above them to fall onto the sidewalk.

definition_simple: A specific piece of land that is officially mapped and can be owned.
definition_technical: A parcel of land defined by metes and bounds, and identified on the city tax map.
why_it_matters: Zoning rules depend on how big your lot is and where it is located on the block.

definition_simple: A permanent roof-like sign that sticks out over a theater or hotel entrance.
definition_technical: A permanent roof-like structure made of metal or glass projecting over an entrance, often used for signage.
why_it_matters: They are heavy and hang over the public; the city requires them to be built extra strong and tested regularly.

definition_simple: A highly experienced professional who is licensed by the city to manage complex electrical work.
definition_technical: A person licensed by the Department of Buildings to perform and supervise electrical work in the city.
why_it_matters: Only a Master Electrician can pull the permits needed for major wiring projects in NYC.

definition_simple: A highly experienced professional who is licensed by the city to manage complex plumbing and gas work.
definition_technical: An individual licensed by the Department of Buildings to perform and supervise plumbing work, including gas piping.
why_it_matters: Only a Licensed Master Plumber (LMP) can pull permits for gas lines and major plumbing systems.

definition_simple: The actual stuff buildings are made of, like concrete, steel, wood, or glass.
definition_technical: Any substance used in the construction, alteration, or repair of a building or structure.
why_it_matters: The city must approve certain materials to make sure they are strong enough and won't catch fire too easily.

definition_simple: Tearing down a building using large machines like excavators or wrecking balls.
definition_technical: Demolition performed with the use of specialized mechanical equipment, subject to specific safety and engineering requirements.
why_it_matters: Much faster than hand demolition but requires more safety plans to protect neighbors from dust and noise.

definition_simple: A single, tall pole used to hold cell phone antennas or power lines.
definition_technical: A type of antenna support structure consisting of a single pole, typically used for wireless communication services.
why_it_matters: They are easier to build than big towers but still need zoning and foundation checks to make sure they won't fall.

definition_simple: A building where three or more families live in separate apartments.
definition_technical: A dwelling which is either rented, leased, let or hired out, to be occupied, or is occupied as the residence or home of three or more families living independently of each other.
why_it_matters: Once a building has 3 units, it must follow much stricter safety laws than a 1 or 2 family house.

definition_simple: When the city officially cancels a violation or stop-work order because the problem was fixed.
definition_technical: The administrative action of closing a violation or rescinding an order following proof of compliance.
why_it_matters: This is the final proof that your building is back in good standing with the city.

definition_simple: Place of Assembly - a special permit for rooms where many people gather, like restaurants or clubs.
definition_technical: An authorization for the use of a space for the gathering of 75 or more persons for purposes such as civic, social, or religious functions.
why_it_matters: Required whenever more than 74 people are in one room to make sure there are enough exits and safety systems.

definition_simple: The formal request to the city to start a construction project.
definition_technical: The official request submitted to the Department of Buildings, including plans and specifications, to obtain a construction permit.
why_it_matters: Gives the city all the details they need to make sure your project will be safe for you and your neighbors.

definition_simple: The whole process of getting the city to approve your construction plans.
definition_technical: The administrative process of reviewing applications and issuing official authorizations for construction activity.
why_it_matters: Can be the longest and most confusing part of a project; doing it right saves months of time.

definition_simple: The master form used to describe a construction project to the Department of Buildings.
definition_technical: A comprehensive form (typically the PW1) used to file plans and work applications with the DOB.
why_it_matters: This form tells the city exactly what you are building and which pros are in charge of the work.

definition_simple: A change made to a building plan after the city has already said 'yes' to the first version.
definition_technical: An application to modify construction documents that have already received Department of Buildings approval.
why_it_matters: Allows owners to change their minds or materials without having to start the whole process over again.

definition_simple: A sign that must be taped to a building or fence to tell neighbors about construction work or hearings.
definition_technical: A mandatory public notice required by law to be displayed at a property site regarding pending permits or land-use actions.
why_it_matters: Gives the public a chance to see what's happening and complain if they think something is unsafe.

definition_simple: Mandatory signs at a construction site that show safety rules and permit info.
definition_technical: Required informational signage at construction sites, including the project's rendering, safety contacts, and permits.
why_it_matters: If these signs are missing, the city can issue an 'easy' violation and fine the owner.

definition_simple: A 'to-do list' at the very end of a project to fix small mistakes or unfinished details.
definition_technical: A document prepared near the end of a construction project listing work that does not conform to contract specifications.
why_it_matters: Helps ensure the owner gets exactly what they paid for before the contractor gets their final payment.

definition_simple: A rooftop that is designed for people to hang out on, like a roof deck or garden.
definition_technical: A roof area designed and intended for use by building occupants for leisure or social activities, subject to specific loading and safety requirements.
why_it_matters: Must have strong floors and high railings to be safe for parties and gatherings.

definition_simple: The vertical tube in high-rise buildings where you drop your trash bags.
definition_technical: A vertical passage in a building through which waste is dropped to a central collection point.
why_it_matters: Must be fire-proof and have sprinklers to prevent a trash fire from spreading through the whole building.

definition_simple: When the city's experts check your plans to make sure they follow all the laws.
definition_technical: The systematic examination of project documents by governmental authorities to verify compliance with codes and standards.
why_it_matters: Catching mistakes on paper is much cheaper than fixing a dangerous building after it is built.

definition_simple: Public land used for streets and sidewalks.
definition_technical: A type of easement granted or reserved over the land for transportation purposes, such as a highway, public footpath, or rail transport.
why_it_matters: You can't build your own stuff on the right-of-way without special city permission because it belongs to everyone.

definition_simple: Large nets hung around high-rise construction sites to catch falling materials or workers.
definition_technical: A net to protect people from injury after falling from heights by limiting the distance they fall, and catching falling debris.
why_it_matters: A critical life-saving device that prevents accidents from becoming fatal tragedies.

definition_simple: Temporary metal platforms that workers use to reach high parts of a building.
definition_technical: A temporary structure on the outside of a building, made of wooden planks and metal poles, used by workers while building, repairing, or cleaning the building.
why_it_matters: They must be built and used perfectly to prevent workers from falling or the platform from collapsing.

definition_simple: The first rough drawings of a building that show the basic shape and size.
definition_technical: The first phase of architectural design, where the architect establishes the general scope and conceptual design of the project.
why_it_matters: Helps the owner decide if they like the overall look of the building before spending money on detailed blueprints.

definition_simple: Detailed drawings made by manufacturers to show how specific parts (like windows or steel beams) will be built.
definition_technical: A drawing or set of drawings produced by the contractor, supplier, manufacturer, subcontractor, or fabricator.
why_it_matters: Architects must check these to make sure the parts will fit perfectly into the overall building design.

definition_simple: Temporary supports used to hold up a building or a wall while work is being done underneath it.
definition_technical: The process of supporting a structure with shores (posts) when it is in danger of collapse or during alterations.
why_it_matters: Prevents the building from collapsing or shifting during renovations or excavations.

definition_simple: The paved path for people walking next to a street.
definition_technical: The portion of a street between the curb lines, or the lateral lines of a roadway, and the adjacent property lines, intended for the use of pedestrians.
why_it_matters: Property owners are responsible for keeping their sidewalks clean and safe (no cracks or ice) to avoid fines and lawsuits.

definition_simple: A law that says people cannot smoke at construction sites.
definition_technical: Legal prohibitions against smoking in designated areas, particularly on construction sites where combustible materials are present.
why_it_matters: Prevents fires from starting in dry wood or trash and keeps the air clean for workers.

definition_simple: A highly trained expert hired to watch very important work, like pouring concrete or welding steel.
definition_technical: A qualified person who demonstrates competence to the satisfaction of the commissioner for the inspection of a particular type of construction or operation.
why_it_matters: They make sure the building's 'skeleton' is strong enough to last for a hundred years.

definition_simple: A construction project where work has stopped for a long time, usually because the owner ran out of money.
definition_technical: A construction site where work has been abandoned or suspended for a period of time, requiring specific maintenance and security measures.
why_it_matters: The city checks these sites extra carefully to make sure the fences and equipment stay safe while nobody is working.

definition_simple: Keeping materials or equipment at a building or construction site.
definition_technical: The act of keeping or placing goods or materials in a warehouse or other designated area.
why_it_matters: Storing dangerous chemicals or too much trash can be a fire risk and lead to violations.

definition_simple: The front part of a store that faces the street, usually with large windows.
definition_technical: The facade of a retail store on the ground floor of a commercial building, typically including display windows.
why_it_matters: NYC has rules about how much of the window must stay clear so that people can see in and the street stays bright.

definition_simple: Using sensors to watch if a building moves or vibrates during construction next door.
definition_technical: The use of various types of sensors to track the structural health and behavior of a building or structure over time.
why_it_matters: Gives an early warning if the work is starting to damage the building so that everyone can stop before it's too late.

definition_simple: Anything that helps hold up a part of a building.
definition_technical: A structural member or system that sustains weights or loads.
why_it_matters: If a support beam or wall is removed without a plan, the whole building can fall down.

definition_simple: A scaffold that is built up from the ground using poles and pipes.
definition_technical: One or more platforms supported by outrigger beams, brackets, poles, legs, uprights, posts, frames, or similar rigid support.
why_it_matters: They must be tied to the building correctly so they don't tip over in high winds.

definition_simple: A scaffold that hangs from the roof on ropes or cables (like for window washers).
definition_technical: A platform suspended by ropes or other non-rigid means from an overhead structure.
why_it_matters: Every part of the cable and motor system must be tested to make sure the platform doesn't fall.

definition_simple: A temporary tube used to slide trash down from high floors into a dumpster.
definition_technical: A temporary enclosed passage used during construction or demolition to convey debris to a lower level.
why_it_matters: Must be very strong so heavy debris doesn't break through and hit people on the sidewalk.

definition_simple: A plan to keep people safe and comfortable if construction is happening in their building while they still live there.
definition_technical: A set of measures designed to protect the safety and health of occupants in a building where construction or alteration work is being performed.
why_it_matters: Ensures that tenants still have water, heat, and safe exits even when the building is being renovated.

definition_simple: A person or company doing professional work (like plumbing or electrical) without having the required city license.
definition_technical: Not having an official license or permission to perform a specific type of professional work.
why_it_matters: Hiring unlicensed workers is risky because they may not know the safety rules and their work could be dangerous.

definition_simple: A building or land that is empty and not being used.
definition_technical: A building or lot that is currently unoccupied and unused.
why_it_matters: Empty buildings can attract squatters or become fire risks if they aren't boarded up and watched.

definition_simple: When the city tells everyone they must leave a building immediately because it is too dangerous to stay in.
definition_technical: An official order from a city agency requiring all occupants to leave a building or specific portion of a building due to hazardous conditions.
why_it_matters: A serious life-saving measure used after fires, structural failures, or major gas leaks.

definition_simple: A security guard who stays at a construction site at night or on weekends.
definition_technical: An individual responsible for monitoring a site during non-working hours to ensure safety and security.
why_it_matters: Required at some sites to prevent fires, stop trespassing, and watch for emergencies while workers are away.

definition_simple: Special permissions needed to build anything near the ocean or rivers.
definition_technical: Permits required for development on or near the city's waterfront, often involving multiple city, state, and federal agencies.
why_it_matters: Protects the city from flooding and makes sure the water stays clean and usable for everyone.

definition_simple: Adding special layers to a building to keep rain and groundwater from leaking inside.
definition_technical: The process of making an object or structure waterproof or water-resistant.
why_it_matters: Essential for preventing mold, wood rot, and structural damage caused by water.

definition_simple: When an owner decides to stop a project and asks the city to cancel their permit application.
definition_technical: The formal retraction of an application or plan that has been filed with the Department of Buildings.
why_it_matters: Officially stops the city from checking the plans and can sometimes get the owner a partial refund on fees.

definition_simple: A drawing that shows how a new building fits within the 'box' of space allowed by zoning rules.
definition_technical: A plan showing the buildable area of a lot, including all applicable yard and setback requirements.
why_it_matters: The city uses this to make sure the building won't be too tall or too close to the neighbors.

definition_simple: A legal document proving who owns a piece of land and which zoning rules apply to it.
definition_technical: An official certification (often a 'Exhibit') that identifies the parties in interest for a zoning lot.
why_it_matters: Required before you can get a building permit for any major new project.

definition_simple: A temporary permission from the city to put something on public land, like a sidewalk clock or a small planter.
definition_technical: A grant of a right to an individual or entity to use city property, typically for a fixed period.
why_it_matters: The city can take this permission back at any time, and you usually have to pay a yearly fee to keep the item there.

definition_simple: A set of technical books and rules that explain exactly how to build things safely.
definition_technical: External codes and specifications that are incorporated into the building code by reference.
why_it_matters: The building code refers to these standards to make sure that materials like concrete and steel are always high quality.

definition_simple: Making sure a building can be used by everyone, including people who use wheelchairs or have trouble seeing or hearing.
definition_technical: The design of products, devices, services, or environments for people with disabilities.
why_it_matters: It's the law; buildings must have ramps, wide doors, and accessible bathrooms so that everyone can use them safely.

definition_simple: Safety nets that stick out from the side of a tall building to catch anything that falls.
definition_technical: A system of nets installed horizontally to catch falling debris or personnel at construction sites.
why_it_matters: Protects people on the street below from falling tools or building materials.
